literal: The offices memorialized that state use was insufficient and firmly asked to restore them; only Su said: "I have heard that if the people are not enough, with whom does the ruler have enough?"
idiomatic: Offices said revenue was short and begged to restore levies; only Su said: "If the people lack, how can the ruler have plenty?"

literal: The emperor approved and followed him.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed and followed him.

literal: Su was eminent in the clan and also aged; the emperor often brought him in and consulted on government; he firmly declined illness and returned home.
idiomatic: Su was a leading kinsman and old; the emperor often consulted him, but he pleaded illness and went home.

literal: Upright by nature, in office fifty years he was the same from start to finish; the age praised him as worthy.
idiomatic: Upright, he held office fifty years unchanged; men called him worthy.

literal: Died; posthumous name Kang; buried at Jinling; honored in the temple hall.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Kang; buried at Jinling; honored in the ancestral hall.

literal: Eldest son Kesiling, seventeen, followed Taiwu hunting and chased a fierce beast; Kesiling then wrestled it barehanded and presented it.
idiomatic: Eldest son Kesiling, seventeen, on a hunt chased a fierce beast and wrestled it barehanded for the emperor.

literal: The emperor said: "Your talent and strength are unmatched—you should build merit for the state; do not do this again!"
idiomatic: The emperor said: "Your strength is rare—serve the state with merit; do not do this again!"

literal: He was at once made Inner Captain Aghan.
idiomatic: He was made inner captain Aghan.

literal: He again followed in pacifying Liangzhou; Juqu Maoxian sent a fierce general to strike Kesiling; both spears broke; Kesiling drew an arrow, shot him, and he fell from his horse.
idiomatic: Pacifying Liangzhou, Maoxian sent a fierce general; both spears broke; Kesiling shot him from the horse.

literal: Kesiling feared rescue would come; before he could draw his sword he used a knife to lever the neck and separate head from body.
idiomatic: Fearing reinforcements, he used a knife on the neck and severed head from body.

literal: The emperor admired him and that same day made him Colonel of the Imperial Garrison and enfeoffed Marquis of Jiyang.
idiomatic: The emperor admired him, made him colonel of the imperial garrison that day, and Marquis of Jiyang.

literal: Died as Commander of the Central Army.
idiomatic: He died as commander of the central army.

literal: Younger brother Peijin inherited the title; for an offense the state was abolished.
idiomatic: Younger brother Peijin inherited; for a crime the fief was abolished.

literal: Peijin's son Zhao, childhood name Ani, was brought in as Palace Gentleman by Director Zhang Yi.
idiomatic: Peijin's son Zhao, called Ani, was made palace gentleman by Zhang Yi.

literal: Xiaowen was to mourn for Prince of Qi Jun Lan, yet Zhao composed palace music.
idiomatic: Xiaowen would mourn Prince Lan of Qi, but Zhao wrote palace music.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "Ani is stupid—who brought him in as gentleman?"
idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Ani is a fool—who made him gentleman?"

literal: Thereupon Yi was demoted to commoner to guard the Masters of Writing; Zhao was stopped and dismissed.
idiomatic: Yi was demoted to commoner guarding the secretariat; Zhao was dismissed.

literal: Under Xuanwu, Zhao's cousin Hui, favored and in power, was gradually moved to Left Vice Director.
idiomatic: Under Xuanwu, cousin Hui rose in favor and Zhao became left vice director.

literal: When Xuanwu died Yu Zhong held government; Zhao was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and again curried favor.
idiomatic: Xuanwu died; Yu Zhong ruled; Zhao was yellow gate gentleman and flattered him.

literal: Zhong monopolized power and wrongly harmed the loyal; much was guided by Zhao.
idiomatic: Zhong seized power and ruined the loyal, often at Zhao's prompting.

literal: When Empress Ling held court he was Director of the Masters of Writing and Intendant of Henan—deaf, fierce, and harsh; affairs were sharp and urgent; wherever he was, men suffered.
idiomatic: Under Empress Ling he was director and Henan intendant—deaf, cruel, and harsh; all suffered where he ruled.

literal: Soon sent out as Inspector of Yongzhou; in the province greedy and brutal, he greatly harmed people.
idiomatic: Soon inspector of Yongzhou; greedy and brutal, he harmed the people.

literal: Later he entered as Director of the Masters of Writing and flattered Liu Teng.
idiomatic: He returned as director and fawned on Liu Teng.

literal: Advanced to General Who Conquers the West.
idiomatic: He was made General Who Conquers the West.

literal: Died; posthumously Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: He bribed Yuan Cha, and therefore the posthumous gifts were unusually generous.
idiomatic: He bribed Yuan Cha, so his posthumous honors were lavish.

literal: Zhao's younger brother Shao, style Choulun, was clever from youth.
idiomatic: Zhao's brother Shao, style Choulun, was clever young.

literal: Moved to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He became right vice director.

literal: Shao in judgment did not avoid the powerful.
idiomatic: Shao judged cases without fearing the mighty.

literal: Xuanwu ordered him to examine Zhao Xiu's prison case; because Xiu was a favorite, he therefore added beating and made him die.
idiomatic: Xuanwu had him review Zhao Xiu's case; Xiu was a favorite, so Shao beat him to death.

literal: The emperor blamed Shao for not reporting first; Shao said: "Xiu's treachery exceeds Dong Xian's; if I did not use the chance to remove him, I feared Your Majesty would again bear Emperor Ai's name.
idiomatic: The emperor blamed him for not reporting; Shao said: "Xiu outdid Dong Xian; if I did not kill him when I could, you might share Emperor Ai's shame.

literal: " Because his words were upright, he was not punished.
idiomatic: His words were just; he was not punished.

literal: On leaving, Prince of Guangping Huai bowed to Shao and congratulated him: "Sir, you are the clan's uprightness—how could Zhu Yun and Ji An look down on you!
idiomatic: Leaving, Prince Huai of Guangping bowed: "You are the house's integrity—Zhu Yun and Ji An cannot match you!

literal: " Shao said: "I only regret the killing came a little late—that is my shame.
idiomatic: Shao said: "I only regret I killed him late—that shames me.

literal: " Died as Inspector of Liangzhou.
idiomatic: He died as inspector of Liangzhou.

literal: Peijin's younger brother Zhong, style Xiande, was known for loyalty and care.
idiomatic: Peijin's brother Zhong, style Xiande, was famed for loyalty.

literal: Under Xiaowen he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director, enfeoffed Duke of Chengyang, added Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the West, with merit in support; the hundred offices all respected him.
idiomatic: Under Xiaowen he rose to right vice director, Duke of Chengyang, palace attendant, and general guarding the west; all offices respected his aid.

literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, gravely ill he resigned and nursed illness at Gaoliu; the imperial carriage personally escorted him beyond the capital gate; attending ministers who took leave all wept.
idiomatic: Taihe year four, mortally ill, he retired to Gaoliu; the emperor escorted him beyond the gate; ministers wept at parting.

literal: When he died all mourned him.
idiomatic: At his death all mourned.

literal: Posthumous name Xuan; ordered the offices to erect a stele inscription.
idiomatic: Posthumous name Xuan; the offices were ordered to set up a stele.

literal: His son Sheng, style Shixing, inherited the title, office: Supervisor of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: Son Sheng, style Shixing, inherited; supervisor of the imperial clan.

literal: Died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Mao, style Boyong, inherited the title, reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: Son Mao, style Boyong, inherited, reduced to marquis.

literal: Following the emperor into the pass he was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping.
idiomatic: He followed the emperor west and was Prince of Beiping.

literal: Died; posthumously Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous name Zhenhui.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously vice director; posthumous name Zhenhui.

literal: His son Zhi, style Jingsheng, Opening Ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Son Zhi, style Jingsheng, opening ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Younger brother Shun, style Jingshu, followed Xiaowu into the pass, enfeoffed Prince of Puyang, office: Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: Brother Shun, style Jingshu, followed Xiaowu west, Prince of Puyang, palace attendant.

literal: When Emperor Wu died the mourning was kept secret; many proposed Prince of Guangping as heir.
idiomatic: When Wu died mourning was secret; many favored Prince of Guangping as heir.

literal: Shun in a side room wept and told Zhou Wen: "Guangping is kin, but in years and virtue he is also full-grown—not fit for the great seat."
idiomatic: Shun wept aside to Zhou Wen: "Guangping is kin, but age and virtue both weigh on him—not for the throne."

literal: Zhou Wen deeply agreed and therefore proclaimed the national mourning and raised the Prince of Nanyang to the imperial title.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen agreed, proclaimed mourning, and raised Prince of Nanyang.

literal: Shun was made Commandant of Justice, acting for Yongzhou, and added Opening Ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and Inspector of Qinzhou.
idiomatic: Shun became commandant of justice, acting for Yongzhou, with opening ceremony rank and Qinzhou.

literal: Shun was skilled at archery.
idiomatic: Shun was a fine archer.

literal: Earlier when Xiaowu was at Luoyang, in Hualin Garden for sport shooting, a silver wine cup holding about two sheng was hung a hundred paces away; more than ten skilled archers shot together—whoever hit received it.
idiomatic: At Luoyang in Hualin Garden a silver cup of two sheng hung a hundred paces; ten archers shot; the hit won it.

literal: Shun loosed an arrow and hit at once; the emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded gold and silk together.
idiomatic: Shun's arrow struck; the emperor rejoiced and gave gold and silk.

literal: Shun then cast a silver boy at the arrow hole, treading a golden lotus, holding skewered meat, and inscribed the back, recording his archery.
idiomatic: He cast a silver boy on the arrow hole, on a golden lotus with skewered meat, and inscribed his skill on the back.

literal: His son Wei, style Ziyou, had pure talent.
idiomatic: Son Wei, style Ziyou, had clear talent.

literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an.
idiomatic: Datong year sixteen he was Prince of Nan'an.

literal: When Yuchi Jiong attacked Shu, Wei was made Recorder; all documents and letters were Wei's work.
idiomatic: When Jiong attacked Shu, Wei was recorder; his was the prose of dispatches.

literal: When the Six Offices were established he was made Junior Master of the Imperial Clan, changed to Duke of Huainan.
idiomatic: Six Offices built, he was junior master of the clan, then Duke of Huainan.

literal: At the start of Zhou Mingdi he was made Senior Master of the Imperial Clan and ordered to collate classics in Qilin Hall.
idiomatic: Ming of Zhou made him senior master and ordered classics collated in Qilin Hall.

literal: Under Jiande he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Minister of Justice, made envoy chief, and returned courtesy to Qi.
idiomatic: Under Jiande he rose to junior minister of justice, envoy chief, and was sent to Qi.

literal: That autumn the emperor campaigned east in person; Wei was then detained by Qi.
idiomatic: That autumn the emperor campaigned east; Qi detained Wei.

literal: When Qi was pacified Wei was released and given Senior Opening Ceremony.
idiomatic: Qi fell; Wei was freed and given senior opening ceremony.

literal: Later made Inspector of Xiangzhou, office: Grand General.
idiomatic: Later inspector of Xiangzhou, grand general.

literal: Wei was gentle and loved quiet; he studied deeply and loved literature.
idiomatic: Wei was gentle, loved quiet, studied, and loved letters.

literal: When he first returned from Ye, Yu Xin gave him a poem: "Liang fell, the hanging jade returned; Qi pacified, the precious tripod came home.
idiomatic: Returning from Ye, Yu Xin wrote: "Liang fell, the hanging jade returned; Qi pacified, the precious tripod came home.

literal: " He was valued by writers thus.
idiomatic: Writers valued him so.

literal: Later he died of illness.
idiomatic: He later died of illness.

literal: Sheng's younger brother Shouxing was clever and loved learning from youth.
idiomatic: Sheng's brother Shouxing was clever and studious young.

literal: At the start of Xuanwu he was Inspector of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: Early Xuanwu he was inspector of Xuzhou.

literal: In office greedy and brutal, he failed the hearts of the people.
idiomatic: Greedy and brutal in office, he lost the people.

literal: His cousin Palace Attendant Hui deeply envied his ability and slandered him to the emperor; an edict ordered Director Cui Liang to gallop and investigate.
idiomatic: Cousin Hui, palace attendant, envied him and slandered him; Cui Liang was sent to investigate.

literal: On the day Liang set out he received Hui's instruction; he then flogged three widows and made them falsely accuse themselves, saying Shouxing had pressed them into servitude.
idiomatic: Liang took Hui's word, flogged three widows, and made them say Shouxing enslaved them.

literal: Shouxing finally feared he could not escape and had his wife's brother Staff Officer Xue Xiuyi take ten carts to move wheat past his confinement.
idiomatic: Fearing doom, he had brother-in-law Xue Xiuyi move ten carts of wheat past his guard.

literal: Shouxing climbed the wall out; Xiuyi put Shouxing in a great wooden box with wheat heaped above and carried him out to Hedong, hiding him in Xiuyi's house.
idiomatic: He climbed out; Xiuyi boxed him under wheat and carried him to Hedong, hiding him at home.

literal: When an amnesty came he came out, saw the emperor, and stated he was slandered by Hui; the emperor did not punish further.
idiomatic: After amnesty he came before the throne and said Hui had slandered him; the emperor did not punish.

literal: Earlier when Shouxing was Junior Mentor, Wang Xian was in the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: Earlier, as junior mentor, Wang Xian was in the eastern palace.

literal: Low in rank, for public business Shouxing flogged him forty strokes.
idiomatic: Low in rank, Shouxing had flogged him forty for public business.

literal: When Xian had favor as Censor-in-Chief he memorialized that at home Shouxing often had resentful words and slandered the court.
idiomatic: When Xian was censor-in-chief he said Shouxing slandered the court at home.

literal: Because the emperor drank to excess and was unaware, he then memorialized; the emperor annotated approval and the order went straight to Shouxing to grant death.
idiomatic: The emperor was drunk and unaware; Xian memorialized; the emperor scrawled approval and Shouxing was ordered to die.

literal: The emperor's writing was half illegible; those who saw it knew it was not his heart, but feared Hui's power and dared not speak.
idiomatic: The note was half illegible; onlookers knew it was not his will but feared Hui.

literal: On the day of execution Xian went in person to watch.
idiomatic: On execution day Xian came to watch.

literal: Shouxing ordered brush and wrote his own epitaph: "A man of Luoyang, surname Yuan given name Jing, had the Way but not the time, his years not long."
idiomatic: Shouxing wrote his epitaph: "A Luoyang man, Yuan Jing by name, had the Way but not the time, his years short."

literal: The rest of the text is mostly not recorded.
idiomatic: The rest is mostly lost.

literal: He turned to his sons and said: "In my coffin put a hundred sheets of paper and two brushes—I mean to sue Xian in the underworld."
idiomatic: He told his sons: "Put paper and brushes in my coffin—I will sue Xian below."

literal: "If Gaozu's spirit knows, within a hundred days he will surely take Xian."
idiomatic: "If Gaozu's spirit knows, Xian will die within a hundred days."

literal: "If there is truly no knowing, what is there to cling to!"
idiomatic: "If spirits know nothing, why cling!"

literal: When Xuanwu died Xian was soon killed.
idiomatic: When Xuanwu died Xian was soon killed.

literal: Shouxing's death—the age also thought it came from the former censor's impeachment of Gao Que and slander.
idiomatic: The age also linked his death to the former censor's attack on Gao Que.

literal: When Empress Ling held court, Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Cui Hong memorialized to clear Shouxing; an edict posthumously cleared him, made Inspector of Yu, posthumous name Zhuang.
idiomatic: Empress Ling's court: Cui Hong cleared him; posthumously inspector of Yu, posthumous name Zhuang.

literal: His son Zui, style Gan, followed Xiaowu into the pass, enfeoffed Prince of Leping, Palace Attendant, concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, added special advancement.
idiomatic: Son Zui, style Gan, followed Xiaowu west, Prince of Leping, palace attendant, left vice director, special advancement.

literal: Shouxing's younger brother Yisheng died young.
idiomatic: Brother Yisheng died young.

literal: Zhong's younger brother De was enfeoffed Duke of Hejian, died as General Who Guards the South, posthumously Inspector of Cao.
idiomatic: Zhong's brother De was Duke of Hejian, died guarding the south, posthumously inspector of Cao.

literal: De's son Ti, Inspector of Yingchuan, died as Inspector of Guang, posthumous name Gong.
idiomatic: De's son Ti was inspector of Yingchuan, died inspector of Guang, posthumous name Gong.

literal: Ti's younger brother Hui, style Jingxi.
idiomatic: Ti's brother Hui, style Jingxi.

literal: Young, deep and keen, he read widely in letters and history.
idiomatic: Young he was deep, keen, and read letters and history.

literal: When Xuanwu succeeded he was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: When Xuanwu succeeded he was yellow gate gentleman.

literal: Earlier when Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang the old nobility all found it hard to move; then wishing to harmonize popular feeling, they allowed winter in the south and summer in the north.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen moved to Luoyang the old nobles resisted; to soothe them they allowed winter in the south, summer in the north.

literal: Xuanwu was quite misled by those at his side; outsiders then had talk of returning north.
idiomatic: Xuanwu was misled by attendants; outsiders spoke of returning north.

literal: It even reached posting notices selling fields and houses, uneasy in their dwellings.
idiomatic: Some posted notices selling land and houses, unsettled in their homes.
